body:
I'm not sure how else this could work. Any time you add an element to the document which is taller than the document, the scrollbars will appear. The canonical fix for this is to use that CSS property that always shows scrollbars, to avoid such issues. But "adjust the spec to avoid reflowing" sounds very weird; are you talking about some kind of pause on the rendering engine that it suspends the normal layout rules for a frame?

Perhaps you were instead thinking about adjusting the default stylesheet for `<dialog>` to be something like `max-height: 100vh; box-sizing: border-box; overflow: auto;`? I think this would be a bit surprising to have dialog behave unlike all other elements in this regard, especially since the effect can be achieved so easily with author CSS. It's not at all obvious to me that this is so universal a design that it should be the default, instead of the simpler option. But I'm willing to be persuaded, and dialog already does have a number of default styles, so maybe that would work?
